title: Design a news feed system like Facebook or Twitter.
description: Personalized feed generation with real-time updates, ranking algorithms, and fanout strategies.

data.text: **Question:** Design a news feed system like Facebook or Twitter.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Generate personalized feed for each user
Real-time feed updates when followed users post
Rank posts by relevance and engagement
Support infinite scroll and pagination
Filter by content type, source, or keywords
Track engagement (likes, comments, shares)

data.title: Scale Assumptions
items: 500 million daily active users
100 million new posts per day
Average feed size: 500 posts
100 million feed generations per second
1 petabyte of post storage annually
Average post size: 200 bytes

data.text: Two main approaches exist for feed generation: fanout-on-write (push model) and fanout-on-read (pull model). Fanout-on-write precomputes feeds when posts are created, while fanout-on-read generates feeds at read time by aggregating posts from followed users.

data.title: Hybrid Approach
data.text: Use fanout-on-write for average users (under 5 million followers) and fanout-on-read for celebrity users. This balances write amplification with read latency.

data.title: Feed Ranking Strategies
items: Recency: Weight posts by creation time
Engagement: Score by likes, comments, shares, and time decay
Affinity: Boost posts from close friends based on interaction history
Machine Learning: Use embedding models to predict user interest
Diversity: Mix content types to avoid filter bubbles

cards.title: Fanout on Write (Push)
cards.description: Precompute feeds when posts are created. Write-intensive, read-optimized.

cards.title: Fanout on Read (Pull)
cards.description: Generate feeds at read time by querying followed users. Read-intensive, write-optimized.

data.title: Horizontal Scaling Strategies
items: Shard feed caches by user_id for horizontal partitioning
Use CDN for static media and popular posts
Rate-limit feed generation per user to prevent abuse
Cache ranked feeds with TTL to reduce computation
Use separate read replicas for feed ranking service

items.question: How do you handle celebrities with millions of followers?
items.answer: Use fanout-on-read for celebrity posts. When a regular user requests their feed, merge the celebrity post with the precomputed feed of other followed users.

items.question: How do you keep feeds fresh?
items.answer: Use a hybrid approach with a short TTL on precomputed feeds and background refresh jobs. For real-time updates, use WebSockets or server-sent events.

items.question: How do you rank posts fairly?
items.answer: Normalize engagement metrics by account age, follower count, and time of day. Use a machine learning model trained on user click-through data.

items.question: How do you prevent feed spam?
items.answer: Implement rate limiting, shadow banning, and engagement quality scoring. Surface high-quality content through ranking rather than chronological order.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Hybrid fanout approaches balance write and read costs
Ranking combines recency, engagement, and user affinity
Shard feed caches by user_id for horizontal scale
Celebrity users require special handling in feed generation
data.takeaway: News feeds require careful trade-offs between write amplification, read latency, and ranking freshness.
